newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Bunds stuck below contract high at 103.52.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Bunds stuck below contract high at 103.52.

text.p: September Bund futures traded on LIFFE are likely to find any upward progress barred by the contract high of 103.52, technical analysts said on Thursday.
Wednesday's trade pushed Bunds to the new high, supported by rising U.S. Treasuries, but analysts said the momentum behind the move is not strong.

"There isn't a lot of upside," said Marc Ostwald, technical analyst at the London Bond Broking company here. "It's run out of steam, and the congestion around 103.47 to 103.52 is the main upside barrier."
September Bunds were up 0.04 at 103.26 by 0650 GMT.

Kathleen Deans, a broker at DMG Futures and Options in Frankfurt said Bunds were targetting 103.69, an extension high, which had to be taken out before the contract could challenge the all-time high at 104.04. On continuation charts, Bunds set the record high on February 18.
Ostwald said that level was under pressure, but the road there would be slow and painful, and Bunds were reliant on continuing strength from the U.S.
"Bunds are going to get there (104.04) at some stage, but it's going to be a crawl," he said. "The market's being driven by the States."
On the downside, Deans said the market would try to fill the gap at the July 22 high of 103.10, left by the previous session's spurt higher. The top of the gap is at Wednesday's low of 103.17.
Oswald said a break of the 103.10 level would target the area of heavy congestion around 102.90/93.
At the short end, December Euromarks were trading up 0.02 at 96.63, with initial resistance pegged at 96.64.
